evals.name: bare-invocation-runs-read-only-check
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check action (the default), reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO/WARN table with one remediation line per finding, and renders nothing.
expectations: Defaults to check when no action argument is given, and never prompts for one
Reads the visualize skill's medium-selection step and the decision matrix it routes to as the source of truth, rather than reciting the setup SKILL.md
Renders nothing: it decides no form, picks no medium for a render, and produces no diagram
Reads the effective medium from the rendered user_config token injected into this skill, and never inspects or edits settings files or pluginConfigs directly

evals.name: unrecognized-medium-warns-and-falls-back-to-auto
evals.prompt: /visualization:setup check — my medium option is set to `artifacts`.
evals.expected_output: WARNs rather than FAILs: the skill reports the unrecognized value and treats it as auto, so nothing is broken. It is a typo whose intended preference silently never takes effect, and this WARN is the only place that surfaces.
expectations: Classifies the unrecognized value as WARN, never FAIL, and states that the skill falls back to auto

Names the full legal set — auto, terminal, file, artifact — and explains that userConfig has no native enum type, so the legal set is validated in-skill and the native configure prompt accepts whatever was typed
States that the intended preference silently never takes effect, and that this report is the only place it surfaces
Prescribes fixing the VALUE, never a change to the skill

evals.name: artifact-preference-inert-when-publish-surface-unreachable
evals.prompt: /visualization:setup check — medium is set to `artifact`. Is that what I will actually get in this session?
evals.expected_output: Crosses the stored preference against live reachability: reports whether the publish surface is actually available to this session rather than assuming it, and when it is not, reports INFO — the render degrades visibly to a local HTML file and then to the terminal — naming the tier that will actually be used.
expectations: Probes whether the Artifact publish surface is reachable in this session rather than inferring reachability from the stored value
When unreachable, reports INFO and names the concrete degradation order: local HTML file, then inline terminal
Names which tier will actually be used in this session, not merely that a fallback exists
Describes the unreachable publish surface as ordinary and documented — plan, sign-in, provider, version and context gating — rather than as a defect to fix
Notes that a mermaid fence in the inline terminal is shown as source, not as a rendered diagram

evals.name: invents-no-prerequisite-and-no-persistent-state
evals.prompt: /visualization:setup check — which binaries does this plugin need, and where does it keep its cached state? Probe them for me.
evals.expected_output: Reports that there is nothing there to probe: this plugin has no external prerequisites, makes no network calls of its own, and keeps no persistent state, so there is no tool to check and no data directory to inspect. Reported as INFO rather than answered with an invented probe list.
expectations: States that the plugin has no external prerequisites, makes no network calls of its own, and keeps no persistent state
Does not invent a binary probe, a data directory, or a cache path the plugin does not have
Describes the chart-craft and artifact-design capabilities as presence-gated collaborators whose absence changes routing and never readiness — not as prerequisites
Reports this finding as INFO

evals.name: apply-refuses-to-hand-edit-the-native-config-surface
evals.prompt: /visualization:setup apply — just set medium to file for me by editing my settings directly.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the hand-edit: medium lives in Claude Code's native configuration surface, which setup must not hand-edit, so apply is verify-and-route. Points at the interactive configure path instead and reports "already configured" when there is nothing to resolve.
expectations: Writes no Claude Code user settings, no pluginConfigs entry, and no plugin-cache file
Routes to /plugin configure visualization@<marketplace> for the interactive path
States that apply is verify-and-route, and that re-running it once the effective medium is legal and reachable changes nothing and reports "already configured"
Does not prompt the user for a choice, because the action was given

evals.name: headless-medium-change-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt: /visualization:setup apply — change medium from artifact to file headlessly. I cannot use the interactive configure prompt from this session.
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless option change to a plain `claude plugin install visualization@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config medium=file` rerun against the already-installed plugin, refuses the uninstall-and-reinstall route, stamps the claim with the CLI version it was verified against, and closes by rerunning check in a fresh session to report the observed effective medium.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install visualization@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config medium=file` rerun, and states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option in the README Options reference table to its manifest default

Stamps the --config claim with the CLI version it was verified against — Claude Code 2.1.240, a non-sensitive option at user scope — and flags a sensitive option and project/local scope as not covered

Tells the operator to pass the scope `claude plugin list` reports for this plugin instead of relying on the -s default of user, and to run from that project's directory for a project or local scope or the write lands at a scope that does not load
Ends by rerunning check in a FRESH session, because the rendered medium token is injected at skill load, and reports the OBSERVED effective medium rather than asserting an unobserved change
